messages.text:
"Create a 3D game gritty, dark third-person stealth-survival game inspired by Manhunt 1 where the protagonist wakes up disoriented after being kidnapped and forced into a brutal, televised underground hunting ordeal inside decaying, claustrophobic night-time urban alleys, shuttered storefronts, damp brick corridors, and dimly lit backstreets lit only by flickering lights and burning trash barrels, wrapped in a paranoid analog VHS camcorder aesthetic with subtle scanlines, grain, and REC HUD overlays. Feature heavy, urgent, slightly hunched third-person running animations with natural arm swing and weapon-in-hand grip variations, smooth crouch-to-sprint transitions, a shadow-stealth system where stepping into deep darkness turns the player invisible to patrolling hunters unless they make noise or collide, and interactive pick-up mechanics allowing the player to scavenge, carry, throw, or perform brutal close-quarters stealth takedowns with makeshift street weapons like knives, wooden bats, bricks, and pipes.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Convert the existing 2D canvas game into a proper 3D, third-person stealth-survival game.

## Requirements
- 3D presentation with a behind-the-player camera.
- Preserve third-person movement, stealth, enemies, pickups, takedowns, weapons, HUD, and VHS styling.
- Maintain support for desktop and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Replaced the canvas 2D renderer with Three.js WebGL.
- Kept gameplay state and mechanics in `index.html`.
- Used direct CDN loading for `three@0.160.0`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built 3D alley geometry, boundaries, walls, shuttered storefront accents, street markings, and brick details.
- Added 3D player, enemy, item, weapon, and barrel meshes.
- Added perspective camera, fog, lighting, shadows, and third-person camera following.
- Preserved stealth detection, patrols, pickups, melee, throwing, health, and HUD behavior.
- Added 3D player crouch and arm/leg animation state.
- Started local server and opened the game in Chromium for verification.
- Captured a verification screenshot at `screenshots/linux.jpg`.

### Active
- Final visual verification of the converted 3D scene.

### Blocked
- "(none)"

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/linux.jpg` and polish any camera, lighting, or scale issues visible in the 3D scene.
2. Test movement, crouching, enemy detection, takedowns, pickups, and throwing in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `[index.html]`: Main and now-converted Three.js 3D game implementation.
- `[screenshots/linux.jpg]`: Latest browser verification screenshot.

## Important Context
- The game uses `import * as THREE from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js';`.
- Local preview server: `http://localhost:3002`.
- The browser verification only reported a missing `favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL software-rendering/read-pixel warnings.
- The active implementation is uncommitted and remains in `index.html`.
